articleTitle: Powering a UAV System Using Photovoltaic Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This study investigates the design and deployment of an energy management system (EMS) for a UA V powered by a combination of photovoltaic cells, a fuel cell, and a lithium-polymer battery. The EMS aims to efficiently manage energy generation, transmission, and consumption to maintain a consistent electrical current, crucial for the UA V’ s consistent operation. It incorporates a control program that utilizes a algorithm to optimize energy use under varying flight conditions, thereby improving the UA V's autonomy and dependability. The EMS has been tested both in the lab and during flights, effectively handling different energy sources and adapting to changes in solar energy, ensuring a steady power supply. The results underscore the significant role of the photovoltaic cells in the UA V’ s energy strategy, facilitating prolonged flights and lessening reliance on batteries. This research highlights the advantages of integrating renewable energy into UA V systems and offers valuable perspectives on expanding their operational range for diverse uses.

articleTitle: Digital Settings of Low Voltage Circuit Breakers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The digital communications networks owned by most electricity companies have undergone remarkable changes. Currently, there are various communication solutions on the market, among the most common are wired and wireless technology. Both technologies are found in applications of electric utility companies, such as the automation of distribution networks, but there is a current concern to digitize these processes. The paper briefly presents the importance of electrical equipment for the protection of installations. Further, some modern features of low-voltage circuit breakers are highlighted. Digital communication networks have different shapes and particularities depending on the application of each equipment. In the final part of the work, the realization of an experimental stand that presents the possibilities of digital communication of low-voltage circuit breakers in a compact version is detailed, as well as specifications of the new generation of low-voltage circuit breakers found in industrial applications. Further, the paper aims to highlight whether the proper functioning of the switch can be affected by its digital parameterization through communication networks.

articleTitle: Some Considerations on the Dimensioning of Ancillary Service Transformers of Power Plants
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: In this paper, the authors present the application of power sizing methods for internal block service transformers through a representative case study of a combined heat and power plant. These complex calculation algorithms were assisted by own calculation programs developed in Mathcad programming environment. Then in order to verify that the chosen transformer ensures the starting or self-starting conditions of the great self-service motors, it is proposed to use simulation models of starting induction motors using the schematic circuit editor in the ANSYS Simplorer interface.

Author Keywords: induction motor starting simulation in ANSYS Simplorer

articleTitle: Development of Electrochemical Method and Unit for the Final Treatment of Carpet Dyeing Production Wastewater
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: Wastewater from carpet/dyeing industries containing a large amount of toxic and biochemically difficult-to-oxidize ingredients poses a serious danger of water and environmental pollution. A fundamental issue in the development of the method of electrochemical water purification was the determination of the role of electrode processes of oxidation and reduction of organic pollutants, methods of electroflotation, coagulation, electrochemical destruction and their combination in order to obtain the maximum treatment effect. The water samples used in experimental studies have been collected after first stage wastewater treatment facility/station of a carpet manufacturing enterprise. The results of the study of the effect of current density on the efficiency and energy consumption of the process of electrochemical final water treatment showed that the highest degree of water treatment effect in the case of combined method electrofiotation-coagulation is achieved in the range of current densities of 20–100 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{A}/\mathrm{m}^{2}$</tex>, and in case of the electrochemical destruction method in the range of 80–200 A/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>•

articleTitle: Towards Sustainable Aviation: Utilizing Range Equations to Optimize Hybrid-Electric Aircraft Propulsion System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The aviation industry faces a pressing need for sustainable solutions to curb its environmental impact. Hybrid-electric aircraft (HEA) present a promising path towards achieving this goal. This paper explores the optimization of HEA propulsion systems by leveraging established range equations. We delve into the application of these equations to model the relationship between HEA design parameters and achievable range. By analyzing the interplay between factors like battery capacity, engine efficiency, and power distribution strategies, the research aims to identify optimal configurations for various mission profiles. This approach promises to maximize the range and efficiency of HEA, ultimately contributing to a more sustainable future for air travel. The paper further explores the limitations of the range equation approach and proposes potential avenues for future research in this domain.

articleTitle: Study of an Aircraft Twin-Spool Single-Jet Turbo-Engine as Controlled Object
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The paper deals with a single-jet twin-spool turbo-engine (TSSJE) for aircraft use. Based on non-linear engine's motion equations, the mathematical model was established. New forms of model's equations were issued, the main input and output parameters were established, as well as the model's coefficients forma. One has studied the variations of TSSJE's essential coefficients (time constants, stability constants, mutual coefficients, particular gains) in the range of engine's operating speeds, but also depending on the flight altitude. Some aspects regarding TSSJE's quality (its time behavior) were also studied using its step response and some important conclusions were drawn.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Remote Controlled Emulator for Standalone PV Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: Immeasurable efforts have been put into strengthening energy security and reducing greenhouse gas emissions by meeting growing energy demand. With declining costs and increasing performance, the deployment of PV systems is growing faster. The focus is on standalone solar photovoltaic systems in rural areas or where grid extension is not feasible. Meteorological conditions impact the standalone PV system's behavior. To avoid critical situations during the PV system operation, it is necessary to implement preventive measures. A PV emulator helps to understand better the behavior of the standalone PV system in critical conditions. This paper presents an intelligent and low-cost PV emulator, with focus on behavior of Li-ion battery, which can be remotely monitored and controlled. The proposed PV emulator consists of: a power supply which has the same behavior as the PV panels, battery storage, consumers which are represented by a electronic load (eload) and remote control functions by using mobile applications. The PV emulator was tested and the behavior of battery was analyzed during the charging and discharging processes. It was determined the capacity of battery is influenced by the values of charging and discharging currents. The ambient temperature influences the internal temperature of Li-ion battery and the PV emulator was stopped when the temperature of Li-ion battery was greater than 53o C.

articleTitle: Simplified Scheme for Longitudinal Control of an Airplane UAV
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This paper proposes a simplified scheme for the longitudinal control of an airplane type UA V. It is intended the scheme to be implemented on board with simple, low cost devices. In most works in literature there are proposed very performing and sophisticated control schemes, studied around a base flight regime. There is the problem to control the UA V on wide domains in the flight envelope, not only in a restricted domain around one base flight regime. Proposed scheme is tested on the non-linear model of the UA V flight dynamics and the results highlight a good behavior for wide flight regime variations.

articleTitle: A Simple Method to Increase Resolution of Trajectory Parameters for 2-DOF Systems Operating in Cyclic Synchronous Position Mode
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: In EtherCAT networks operating in Cyclic Syn-chronous Position (CSP) mode, drive systems typically receive only position reference from the master. In cost-sensitive applications, where controlled motors are equipped with low-resolution position sensors, using simple differentiation to obtain velocity and acceleration commands from position reference leads to signals of poor resolution. Subsequently, these signals cannot be reliably used in the feedforward part of a two degrees of freedom (2-DOF) control scheme. This paper presents a simple method to improve the resolution of the velocity and acceleration command signals when computed only from position reference. The proposed solution leads to control performances similar to cases where the velocity and acceleration commands are com-puted accurately using a drive's built-in trajectory generator. Two additional filtering options are detailed. Practical experiments demonstrate the viability of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Digital System for High Power Synchronous Motor Excitation Control
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The use of synchronous motors in variable speed drives for the simultaneous generation of mechanical power and reactive power is one of the most advantageous methods of improving the power factor in electrical distribution networks. The use of automatic excitation control has extended the application of synchronous motors to high load shock drives. The digital control and regulation systems developed to control the excitation of synchronous motors are modern solutions that restore the relevance of synchronous machines. This paper presents a fully digital solution for the design of equipment to supply excitation and control the operation of high power synchronous motors, which can be easily parameterized for low and medium voltage synchronous motor drives of various rated powers, with asynchronous starting capability.

articleTitle: Computing the Parameters of the Impedance Circuit Matching
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The paper introduces an efficient method for analytical computation of the matching circuits parameters based on the maximum active power transfer theorem. For T or Pi circuit configurations, which have more than two parameters, the theorem provides two independent equations with the parameters as variables. Since T or Pi circuits have three parameters, one parameter must be chosen arbitrarily. It is then necessary to verify that this chosen value, along with the other two parameters, achieves proper impedance matching for analog circuits or signal transmission networks.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Locking/Releasing System for UAVs Wireless Charging Stations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: A drone is an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) controlled from the ground by an operator. These vehicles have been under strong development in the last decade both for civil/commercial (surveillance of overhead power lines, territory mapping, fast transports over short distances, PV power plant supervision, fertilizer spreading in agriculture etc.) and military purposes. A main feature of these drones is their action range. This feature is limited by the weight and capacity of the current batteries, which is why it is necessary to recharge them frequently. So far, in-flight battery charging or quick automatic battery swapping on the ground have not been applied. Instead, ground charging is used through conductive technology with galvanic contact or wireless technology. Galvanic contact is affected by difficult atmospheric conditions (wind, rain, snow, mud). This paper presents a novel electromagnetic system that is able to lock the drone on the charging station during wireless charging and to release it at the end of the process.

articleTitle: A Low-Cost Baro-Altimeter Model with Piezoresistive Sensor and Commercial Off-the-Shelf Components
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: One of the most important parameters managed during the flight of an aero-vehicle is its barometric altitude. Depending on the aero-vehicle type, the used method for its determination can vary. The conventional method uses an aneroid capsule as sensitive element, but the development of technology has led to electronic versions. One of the variants is the one with piezoresistive sensor. The paper proposes a simple low-cost solution, with commercial off-the-shelf components, based on a piezoresistive sensor and a programming board. The calibration according to the equation of the dependence between altitude and atmospheric pressure, and the laboratory testing, although in the preliminary stage, led to promising results. A stand-alone baro-altimeter variant based on the same configuration is also proposed. Having in mind that the test results here provided refer at low altitudes, under 1600 m, an immediate application identified for our system is for low altitude drones.

articleTitle: Automation System for Testing Air Turbine Starters for Naval Gas Turbines
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The paper presents the automation system developed for the testing bench of air turbine starters. The starters were designed and developed for starting-up Pratt & Whitney ST40M gas turbines installed on-board of the Romanian frigates. During the naval retrofitting works conducted by the Romanian Research and Development Institute for Gas Turbines COMOTI, the former cruise engines were replaced with P&W ST40M gas turbines, which require lightweight, compact and reliable starters. A total of eight air turbine starters were designed, developed and tested, four installed on the four ST40M gas turbines on both frigates power transmission lines and four as spare ones. To ensure a flawless, reliable operation of the starters on gas turbines, the test bench has to include the necessary equipment and instrumentation integrated in the automation system. An electric generator was considered to act as a brake and simulate the load of the gas turbine. The starter needs between 25–45 seconds to start-up the gas turbine on-board. The main parameters that were observed during the bench tests are: starter speed, motor speed and power, vibration levels, air and oil pressure, and temperature. Thermographic scanning was also conducted, observing the temperature decrease at starter's turbine in its operation modes.

articleTitle: Electric Diagram for the Study of Series Electric Arcs Fault
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: Electric arc faults in series with the load in a single-phase alternating current circuit are difficult to detect due to the decrease in the effective value of the current when they occur. At the same time, they are extremely dangerous because of the possibility of producing fires caused by an electrical fault. Electric arc detection devices are the only electrical protection devices able to detect and interrupt the supply of circuits when this type of fault occurs. To study the operation of these protective devices, a laboratory electric diagram is proposed, through which two types of electric arc faults are simulated. The electrical parameters measured are the discharge voltage, the electric current through the arc and the derivative of the noise produced by the electric arc.

articleTitle: Extracting Small-Signal Models of Power Converters Using Time-Domain Step Response Simulation in SPICE
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This document presents a simple method for using time-domain simulations to extract an AC small-signal model of the power stage in a power converter. Such extraction is important for simulating feedback loop gain and assessing the stability of complex power converter topologies, such as resonant converters or converters with advanced switch control. With the proposed approach, a single time-domain simulation run is sufficient to extract the small-signal model, making the process time-efficient. The method is based on step response simulation, where the input control signal (e.g., duty cycle, switching frequency) is applied as a step function. The output parameter of the converter (such as output voltage or current) is recorded during the time-domain simulation and then converted into a SPICE netlist using Laplace transform statements. The Laplace transform in the s-domain is supported by most SPICE simulators, including LTspice and PSpice. The presented algorithm and model are automatically generated using an open-source software tool. Thus, free tools like LTspice, combined with the open-source tool, can serve as cost-effective alternatives to commercial SPICE programs such as PSpice, PADS, Simetrix, and MATLAB.

articleTitle: Device for Passive Rehabilitation of Knee and Hip Joints with an Arduino Microcontroller
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This paper is related to the development of a low-cost device for rehabilitation of knee and hip joints. Based on the formulated requirements the main steps of the device development are described. The necessary calculations for the mechanical part of the device are presented. A number SolidWorks models are developed for different positioning angles of the construction. A hybrid stepping motor is selected to drive the device, which is controlled by an Arduino microcontroller. The practical implementation is illustrated for some typical use cases of the device. The research carried out and the results obtained can be used in the development and application of such type of devices for passive rehabilitation of knee and hip joints.

articleTitle: Dynamic and Adaptive Control of Monoaxial GS with GAR. Part 2: Control Architecture Design and Validation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This paper presents the design of adaptive control subsystems of the precession angle of the gyroscope-inner gimbal assembly and of the angular velocity of rotation of the platform (outer gimbal) from the monoaxial force GS component with GAR. The nonlinear dynamics of the two stabilization and guidance subsystems were obtained in the first part of this paper series. The design of the two subsystems is based on the use of the concept of dynamic inversion and neural networks. The control structures include reference models, dynamic compensators (P.I. and, respectively, P.D.), linear state observers and neural networks. Neural networks model the adaptive components of the control laws, these having the role of compensating dynamic inversion errors. By numerical simulation, using Matlab/Simulink models of the two subsystems, the dynamic GS characteristics for stabilization and orientation regimes are drawn.

articleTitle: SPD Miscoordination in PV Systems Due to Lightning Strikes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This study deals with the coordination of surge protection devices (SPD) in photovoltaic systems (PV). A PV farm model was developed in MATLAB Simulink with all the main components, solar panels, converter, grounding system, power transformer, cables in the DC and AC branches with their capacitances, and surge protection device throughout the installation. It was found that when lightning strikes the grounding system or in the vicinity of the PV installation, the coordination among SPD types 1, 2, and 3 is lost. Miscoordination can cause damage to several elements of the PV system, mainly the inverters. Finally, solutions were proposed to avoid SPD miscoordination during lightning strikes.

articleTitle: Fault Detection in Electric Motors using Acoustic Signals and Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The classification of sound signals can be applied to the fault diagnosis of electromechanical devices and systems, such as electrical machines, drives, production machines, etc. Traditional methods identify acoustic signals by analyzing their characteristics in both the time and frequency domains. This paper focuses on one of the latest trends for visualizing sound signals which can then be used by image classification models for fault detection in electrical machines and drives. The experiment described uses an electric motors sound recording dataset together with Domain Generalization approach based on Symmetrized Dot Pattern. Image classification is utilized to distinguish the different conditions of the electric motors. The results suggest that the presented approach could be a fast and cost-effective method for electrical machine diagnostics. Despite the promising outcomes, further work can be done based on more versatile data and different image classification models relying on autoencoders or convolutional neural networks together with large language models.

articleTitle: Experimental Study of the Behaviour of Distribution Transformers Under Short-Circuit Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: An important part of the design of power transformers is based on short circuit behaviour. This paper presents an experimental study of a transformer with circular concentric coils, using metal foil as a conductor in the low voltage winding, with a rated power of 2000 kVA.

articleTitle: Electromechanical Transient Process in a Three-Phase Cage Induction Motor Due to Sudden Step Change in Supply Voltage Frequency
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: In this paper, electromechanical transient process occurring in a three-phase cage induction motor due to a sudden step change in frequency of the time-harmonic supply voltage is analyzed using small-signal linearized complex differential equations of the motor dynamic model. The electromechanical transient analysis is corroborated by case-study numerical results.

articleTitle: Dynamic and Adaptive Control of Monoaxial GS with GAR. Part 1: Obtaining the Nonlinear Dynamic Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This paper series presents a study on the dynamics and adaptive control of a monoaxial force gyro stabilizer (GS) with rapid astatic gyroscope (GAR) using the concept of dynamic inversion and neural networks. In part 1, using a nonlinear mathematical model of the GS, the nonlinear dynamics of the stabilization and orientation subsystems are decoupled, the relative degrees of the output variables are calculated, and their inverse dynamics. The coupling coefficient between the two nonlinear dynamics is calculated from stability conditions. This coefficient express the dependence between the precession angle of the GAR and the orientation angular velocity of the platform (outer frame), and allows for the decoupled control of nonlinear dynamics of stabilization and orientation. Part 2 contains the design and software validation of the dynamic inversion based control arhitectures.

articleTitle: Study of Biconical Antenna Behavior Using CST Software
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This paper presents a study on the behavior and design of a biconical antenna within the frequency range of 250–750 MHz, conducted using the CST learning edition software. Because the number of IoT and 5G+ devices increase, so does the unintended interaction between these devices, as well as interference with older devices operating at lower frequencies. This phenomenon is known as electromagnetic interference (EMI). Thus, there is a need for a wideband device that covers several octaves. A thoroughly researched solution is the biconical antenna. Current and older designs of biconical antennas can be improved to meet the requirements of 5G+ devices

articleTitle: Behavior of a Traction Induction Motor with Rotor Flux-Oriented Control
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: Field-oriented control has proven its viability and superiority in electric power systems, including electric traction. This paper is focused on the implementation of the rotor flux-oriented control with voltage control on a traction induction motor. Firstly, the control scheme and calculation fundamentals are presented. Then, the performance of the system in dynamic and steady-state regimes is presented by simulating the operation of a real traction motor at two prescribed speeds, taking into account the passage of wheels over the rail joints, which is a phenomenon specific to electric locomotives. A low speed (about 20 % of the nominal speed) and the highest speed (about 160 % of the nominal speed) are taken into consideration. It is shown that all the controlled quantities follow the prescribed values well, the peak current through the motor is below the limiting value and the switching frequency is below the imposed limit. Also, the performance in steady-state regime is good.

articleTitle: Specificity of the Behavior of a Newly Designed Traction Electric Motor for Driving Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The dynamic behavior of an electric drive with a newly designed traction induction motor has been studied. The focus has been on the influence of the total moment of inertia parameter on the resulting impact torques and currents, also for the startup time. Some types of losses have been calculated also. The results obtained from the research have been given tabularly and graphically. Concluding comments have been done.

articleTitle: Design Considerations for Switched-Mode Power Supplies with Capacitive Coupling
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: Switched-mode power supplies (SMPS) typically utilize optical couplings via optocouplers or inductive couplings with pulse transformers to close the feedback loop. To enhance the performance of SMPS and reduce production costs, this paper explores design considerations by replacing the inductive and optical couplings with a capacitive coupling. The capacitive coupling is formed from the PCB wiring of the power supply and its incorporated copper layers. The performance of the modified SMPS is evaluated through computer simulations, followed by the construction of a physical prototype based on the proposed design and calculations. The presented solution offers several advantages, such as: it improves temperature stability, leading to less variation of key parameters due to temperature fluctuations or it lowers manufacturing costs by eliminating the need for optocouplers or transformer cores in favor of a capacitive coupling circuit.

articleTitle: Wireless Communication for SCADA System of a Railway Electrical Substation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The aim of this paper is the implementation and validation of the wireless communication in a The Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition system (SCADA). The implementation was done for an electrical substation, in order to optimize the time in which the user intervenes within the electrical substations to make the required improvements and to optimize the costs with the trips to the electrical substation a wireless connection method is approached.

articleTitle: Modeling and Simulation of Unit Heat Flux and Temperatures for a Multilayer Wall Using Ansys
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The aim of this paper is to perform a numerical analysis and steady-state modeling of the unit heat flux and temperature variations for different multilayer wall structures. The present work aims to determine the numerical values and simulate the unit heat flux and temperatures for six types of wall structures using ANSYS 2024Rl software, thereby determining which of the analysed structures is the most thermally efficient. The multilayer wall structures analysed are made of concrete, aerated concrete and brick, and the insulation layers used are polystyrene and mineral wool.

articleTitle: Enhancing Photovoltaic Efficiency: Optimal Tilt Angle Estimation Using Advanced Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This study explores the enhancement of the tilt angle of photovoltaic (PV) systems using both traditional empirical models and advanced machine learning techniques. Traditional methods, including second-degree polynomial, third-degree polynomial, and Fourier series models, were implemented and evaluated. In addition, advanced machine learning algorithms such as model-agnostic meta-learning (MAML), automated machine learning (AutoML) using TPOT, and transfer learning with domain adaptation were applied to optimize the tilt angle. The research aims to demonstrate the potential advantages of using sophisticated machine learning approaches over conventional methods.

articleTitle: Transformer Fault Detection Using DGA Based on Three Ratio Technique and Random Forest Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: Power transformers are essential elements in the production and distribution of electricity, and keeping them in optimum operating condition is a constant concern for specialists in the field. The condition of power transformers is mainly determined by the condition of the mixed insulation system, i.e. solid cellulose paper insulation and liquid insulating oil insulation. This is why the Three Ratio Technique (TRT) is used with good results for the early detection of power transformer faults. In this paper, the ratios defined by the TRT method are used to train a machine learning classifier based on ensemble and random forest algorithms. The validation of the power transformer fault identification software application for the proposed method is carried out in the experimental section.

articleTitle: Mechanically Driven Pump Versus Electrically Driven Pump for Fuel Systems of Jet Engines
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: Jet engines for aircraft use are mandatorily assisted by fuel installations (fuel control units - FCUs); their main equipments are the pumps, whose drive can be done mechanically or electrically, depending on the engine's designer and manufacturer choice. The paper comparatively analyzes the behavior of jet engines as controlled objects in both pump drive cases. Starting from the mathematical models of pumps, of jet- engines and of their controllers, studies were carried out regarding the time response of the embedded systems, variation graphs concerning engine's main output parameter(s) were drawn and, finally, some important conclusions were obtained.

articleTitle: Proactive Monitoring and Protection of Battery
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: Nowadays electrical batteries become more used in a large area of activities. We have used batteries as power sources for different equipment and storage of supplementary energy produced by green energy sources (eolian or solar). All actual batteries have a Battery Management System module included. We propose an advanced module, Battery Monitoring System (BMoS), that monitors the status of the battery, and the work conditions, and more than this, the module will be able to disconnect the battery to avoid any damage. The BMoS is small and can be included in the battery pack along with BMS.

articleTitle: Computer Aided Design of Two-Element Matching Network Using the ZY Smith Chart
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: Impedance matching is a crucial concept in electrical engineering and electronics, aiming to optimize power transfer between analogue circuits and transmission lines. This paper explores the significance of impedance matching techniques in various applications, highlighting their impact in system performance and efficiency. It presents a computer aided design procedure that calculates the values of components needed to fulfil the condition of impedance matching using Smith chart.

articleTitle: Disturbance Observer and Adaptive Robust Control for PMSM Drive Using MRAS-Based Parameters Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This paper proposes an adaptive robust control strategy for permanent magnet synchronous machine based on speed and currents disturbance observation. The suggested approach uses the model reference adaptive system to estimate the motor's parameters that are needed to tune the controllers. However, a significant challenge arises due to the variation of motor parameters which impact the speed and current control when the temperature increases. The proposed robust control technique combines cascaded controllers, resistance, inductance and flux linkage estimation to ensure accurate regulation of stator currents and rotor speed. Including an adaptive system for parameters variations, the proposed model helps to compensate the control errors and to maintain the system performance. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed adaptive robust control strategy.

articleTitle: Protothread and Cooperative Multitasking Scheduler on the Arduino Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: In the search for a simple and scalable firmware solution for Internet of Things (IoT) applications on devices with significant constraints, such as limited energy, hardware resources, and cost, numerous well-recommended and widely used solutions, including Contiki and RIOT, can be identified. Despite their merits, these solutions often present challenges when deployed on popular boards, such as the Arduino or ESP32/8266. This paper synthesizes diverse experiences and introduces idOS, a cooperative task scheduler featuring protothreads, timers, power management, and a TCP/IP network stack atop the Arduino framework, with a particular focus on users interested in IoT applications. This work examines the motivations, philosophy, structure, and limitations of idOS, offering insights into its development and potential applications.

articleTitle: Mathematical Aspects on the Phase Shift Network of RC Oscillators
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: Audiofrequency generators are frequently used both as independent circuits and as components of various electronic devices. In this paper, the study focuses on one of the components of RC type oscillators, respectively on the feedback network. This has an important role in terms of ensuring a certain phase shift between the output signal and the input signal. In addition to this aspect, other quantities were also deduced, such as the attenuation of the output signal and the cut-off frequency. The influence of the number of RC-type stages was analyzed, too. The calculations were done analytically, in order to obtain accurate results. The numerical values obtained analytically for a case study were compared with the numerical results given by a specialized circuit simulation software. The conclusions confirm the statements made in specialized works.

articleTitle: Exploring the Impact of Shading on the Efficiency of Photovoltaic Panels - Part II
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The use solar photovoltaic technology, as one of renewable sources for energy production, is currently experiencing a strong development all over the world, being a sustainable, environmentally friendly, affordable, and easy to implement solution. The amount of energy produced, and the efficiency of photovoltaic panels are influenced by a series of factors that can be intrinsic, external, or environmental. To increase the efficiency of photovoltaic panels and their lifespan, it is important that the parameters with a direct influence be taken into consideration. These influencing factors include ambient temperature, solar panel temperature, direct solar irradiation, wind speed, altitude, atmospheric pressure, and local stressors such as shading, dust accumulation and pollution. Among them shading has been identified as a significant concern. Shading, either permanent or temporary, can significantly reduce the electricity generation capacity of photovoltaic panels. This article aims to investigate the impact of shading on a photovoltaic panel's performance, focusing on parameters such as output power, voltage and electrical current, as well as its efficiency. Through a series of computational simulations and experimental investigations, the research quantifies the impact of partial cell shading while also exploring photovoltaic panels shading mitigation strategies.

articleTitle: Modeling and Simulation of the Variation of the Thermal Flux Yielded by a Medium Temperature Radiant Panel Using Matlab - Simulink
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: Nowadays, the issue of efficient heating of enclosed spaces where people carry out different activities has become a priority. This means, on the one hand, using the cheapest and least polluting thermal energy and, on the other hand, using high-performance energy equipment that transmits heat energy as efficiently as possible from the heat carrier (thermal agent) to the air inside the space to be heated. One such heating system is medium-temperature radiant panel heating using thermal agents. In this paper, starting from a specific construction type of a radiant panel, a study is carried out, using Matlab - Simulink, on the variation of the heat flux transmitted by a medium temperature radiant panel using thermal agent at different temperatures. The modelling algorithm transposed into the simulation scheme in Matlab - Simulink allows a quick and relevant analysis of the behaviour of such a decentralised heating system when operating in rooms with different thermal regimes.

articleTitle: From Model Predictive Control to Data Driven Control to Meet High Efficiency Objective of a PMSM Drive System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: In this paper is proposed a Data Driven Control (DDC) law of a Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine (PMSM) drive as an alternative to the Model Predictive Control (MPC) strategy. The DDC method is designed for the inner control structure of the PMSM drive, the outer speed loop being employed by a classical linear PI controller. Thus, the DDC is based on build up a database of the relevant quantities as electromagnetic torque, speed, voltages and current, all obtained in steady - state regime with MPC strategy, being selected for the highest efficiency values for a given pair of speed and torque. The learning process of the DDC strategy by a mutidimesional interpolation method leads to obtain high performances in both steady - state and dynamic regimes, without any additional optimal current reference command. A comparative analysis done in Matlab simulation environment of the results obtained by both MPC and DDC control laws shows the effectiveness of the last strategies. The DDC method provide a robust optimal control under energetic constraints, being more suitable then the classical MPC law that can not offers reliable results for a large area of conditions in practice.

articleTitle: Regeneration of Waste Oils in Electrical Equipment in Accordance with EU Regulations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This paper presents the first phase of the project initiated by the authors to find an optimal solution for the regeneration of waste oils from electrical equipment, bringing their parameters into line with those of type B oils as defined in the lEC 60296:2020 standard. In this first stage, two paraffin- based mineral oils without additives, with different degrees of degradation/aging, collected from electrical equipment with an age in service of approximately 38 years, and three adsorbents were used to determine the ability of each to improve the physical and chemical properties of waste oils. The experiments showed that all the adsorbents used significantly reduced the moisture concentration and eliminated a significant part of the oil acid degradation products (polar elements), thus significantly improving the properties of the oil subjected to the treatment process.

articleTitle: Rotor Field Quasi-Oriented Control Algorithm Implementation for Railway Traction Systems on dSPACE DS1103
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The aim of this paper is the experimental implementation and validation of a rotor field quasi-oriented control algorithm for a railway vehicle traction system. The implementation was done for a dSPACE DS1103 prototyping board in the Matlab Simulink environment. The control system assumes that the current system is oriented by the rotor flux and that the real flux follows the imposed value. This way the estimation of the rotor flux is not necessary making the control algorithm suitable for low cost industrial DSP applications. The drawback is given by the fact that the current projections on the dq axes cannot be regulated directly, but only by means of the current phasor magnitude. The proposed control system proved good results, in terms of current and speed regulation especially at variable mechanical load (such as track joints or switches), both in static and dynamic regimes, but some precautions must be taken at null imposed speed as the minimum frequency of the magnetizing current leads to a slow rotation of the idle motor.

articleTitle: Mixed Reality Application in Robot Navigation and Control
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: Among the emerging technologies, Mixed Reality (MR) has provided the means to interact with holograms. A very distant future is now near and accessible, which allows for the replacement of classic controllers for robots and is driven by MR. Holograms involve dynamic 3D elements that are integrated into the environment, enhancing control means for the user. These elements may be visually attended to and interacted with via eye concentration or hand gestures, and they have the capability to execute a variety of activities. This emerging technology enables interactions that are otherwise unattainable in alternative settings or contexts, such as the presence of an avatar inside the program. Furthermore, it has the potential to be expanded to govern other mechatronic devices, including robots. The purpose of this work is to offer an improved and interactive method of controlling a mechatronic platform by using holograms, such that the adaptability of this technology may be shown in the context of operating real systems. Important for the authors of this paper is the broadening of the spectrum in which the application lies, thus contributing to the process followed for the development and applicability of the solution in key areas such as industry, training, and medicine.

articleTitle: Optimizing Underwater Imaging through Wavelength Adjustment of Light Sources: A Case Study at the Black Sea Using EPS Vision 1712
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This study explores methods to optimize the quality of underwater images by adjusting the wavelength of light sources, with specific applications to the Black Sea. Utilizing the EPS Vision 1712 equipment, equipped with a high-resolution camera and an adjustable LED lighting system, the study analyzes the influences of environmental parameters such as turbidity, temperature, depth, and salinity on light propagation and underwater image quality. Additionally, techniques for automating the lighting optimization process are explored to improve the efficiency and accuracy of underwater inspections. Future research directions include integrating environmental sensors and developing adaptive algorithms for dynamic control of light sources.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Corona in Partial Discharge and Radio Interference Measurement Circuits
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The paper presents how the physical phenomenon, corona discharge, can be evaluated using circuits for measuring partial discharges and radio disturbances. The main features and differences between these circuits are presented, which include the measurement systems and their calibration methods. In a test circuit simulating the occurrence of corona discharges, corona discharges were evaluated at different test voltages using the same measurement frequencies for the two systems. The UV spectrum and the electric field of these discharges are correlated with the applied voltage.

articleTitle: Development of a Time Domain Reflectometer Application Using Matlab/Simulink for Detecting Faults in Electrical Cables
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The paper presents an application of a time domain reflectometer, using a Simulink model and Matlab App Designer intended to explore the importance of proper use of the real time domain reflectometer equipment. To highlight the usefulness of this application, the information presented in the paper is divided into four sections. The introductory section is devoted to the need to maintain the integrity of electrical cables in good condition. In the second section a time domain reflectometer equipment and its operating principle are described. The development of a friendly interactive interface of a time domain reflectometer model is detailed in the third section. Finally, in the last section is emphasized the use of the proposed application.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning using NI AutoML in Industry - Case Study: Simulated Waveforms
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: Nowadays, Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning is everywhere, and everyone wants to use it. This paper presents a case study on how to use NI AutoML application to more easily solve a waveforms prediction problem. NI AutoML is a web application that allows layman, and also data scientist, to train Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning models as a self-service. The paper presents a simple and basic example that can be further developed and add more complexity on top of it for being applied in real industrial problems such as the battery industry where in the test step the current and the voltage are measured and analyzed to know if the battery is good or bad. The presented case study is just a simple example of this complex problem. Instead of data from the battery, it used data from an RL simulated circuit and obtained waveforms from current and voltage. The data was loaded into NI AutoML and created a prediction model, that was used in NI SystemLink Enterprise into Jupyter Notebook for calculating the prediction for new data that arrived into the system and in the end, all the predicted results are presented into one NI SystemLink Dashboard.

Author Keywords: artificial intelligence and machine learning algorithms

articleTitle: Multi-parameter Analysis of Active Energy Consumptions in a Municipal Hospital
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The paper deals with the multi-parameter analysis of active energy consumptions in a Romanian municipal hospital. Minimum, mean, and maximum values are computed based on measurements recorded every 15 minutes by the energy provider, the analyzed time range being between the 1-st of July 2021 and the 30-th of June 2022. The analysis delved into monthly, daily, and hourly consumption trends. The investigation extended to seasonal variations, to discern the impact of climatic conditions. The study also differentiated between working and non-working days, recognizing the dynamic energy demands during operational and non-operational periods. Peak hours are examined to pinpoint instances of heightened consumption, providing valuable insights for optimizing resource utilization. Synthetic conclusions with respect to different categories of consumptions are provided. A solution based on photovoltaic panels is suggested in the end, along with the estimation of the time required for the full return of investment.

articleTitle: Analyzing Analog Signal Transmission over Optical Fibers using Pulse Width Modulation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: Nowadays, digital technology has developed new techniques of signal processing. In this work, we studied the analog signal transport through optical fiber using PWM modulation. For this, we present a comparative analysis of our study on methods of analog signal processing (conversion and restoration) using digital or analog technology. Here we have presented conversion methods using digital circuits and circuits based on analog signal processing using FPAAs. Using FPAAs creates an opportunity to increase the degree of integration of signal processing solutions and minimize the electronic circuits. In the work, we used standard optical fiber digital communication interfaces. From the experimental results, we note that FPAA technology can be used alongside digital technology in the processing of analog signals, increasing processing speed and decreasing the integrated circuit area.

articleTitle: Energy Community for Condominium Members
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The paper aims to present the ways of realizing an energy community within a condominium with 55 apartments. The case study presents an example of an energy community that manages the production of renewable energy by placing photovoltaic systems on the roof for the common consumers of the condominium, but also proposals for an energy community in which a part of the individual consumption of each apartment is ensured. Also, the legislative, technical and financing barriers existing at the moment in the development of energy communities within condominiums were presented.

articleTitle: Optimization by Zooms Without and with Second-Order Polynomial Models Applied to a 2-D Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: In this paper, the optimization method by zooms based on the design of experiments concept is presented, in two variants. The first variant only requires access to the values of the objective function at different points in the feasible domain, grouped in designs of successive experiments, oriented towards the most convenient values. The second variant additionally calculates second-order polynomial models that approximate the objective function on each design, facilitating the increase of the convergence speed of the algorithm. The two variants fit very well with the numerical simulations by the finite element method. Therefore a comparative study of their application on a bi-dimensional numerical model of an electromagnetic device is presented. The results highlight the simplicity of the first variant but also the high convergence speed of the second one.

articleTitle: Embedded Application for Power Flow Variability Assessment
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The evaluation of low voltage (LV) distribution power grids needs precise power profiles not only for installed power generation, including renewable sources but also for individual and combined loads. Traditional power system analysis methods generally operate under the assumption of a steady-state condition between consecutive measurements. To verify the assumption that the system conforms to this predefined model, statistical metrics can be used. In this paper, some of these metrics (CV(RMSD) and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R^{2}$</tex>) are integrated as part of an application that can be embedded in state-of-the-art smart meters.

articleTitle: Aspects Regarding the Testing of an ONAN Distribution Transformer with a Special Construction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The paper is focused on the testing of a special distribution transformer with the following rated data: 250 kVA – 20 (10) kV/ 0,4 kV, Dyn5 connection, type of cooling system- ONAN. It is intended to be connected in the electrical distribution networks, where currently the rated voltage of this networks is 10kV, but in the future the voltage will increased at 20 kV. A series of the test results after the construction of the transformer are presented.

articleTitle: Analysis on the Behaviour of 36 kV, 10 kA Pre-failed Polymer Surge Arrester at Short-Circuit Current
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: In order to study the behaviour of metal oxide surge arresters at short-circuit current, this paper presents an experimental study on four pieces of 36 kV, 10 kA surge arresters at different values of short-circuit current. Prior to the experiments, each surge arrester was electrically pre-faulted with a power frequency overvoltage without any physical modification The tests were carried out under severe conditions at rated short-circuit current, the peak value of the first half cycle of the actual arrester current was at least <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sqrt{2}$</tex> times the RMS value of the rated short-circuit current.

articleTitle: A Low-Cost Microwave Hybrid Biosensor for Glucose Concentration Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This study uses a hybrid biosensor consisting of a patch antenna with a defected ground plane and a frequency-selective surface (FSS) to detect glucose concentration in the microwave frequency region. The sensing mechanism is based on identifying the relative permittivity and loss tangent variations caused by different ratios of glucose-distilled water solutions placed in the area of the sample under test (SUT). This study tested four glucose-distilled water solutions in the SUT region: 72 mg/dL, 216 mg/dL, 330 mg/dL, and 600 mg/dL. The Debye model is utilized to ascertain the dielectric characteristics of the solutions. When the volume percentage of glucose in the glucose-deionized water solutions in the SUT increased from 72 mg/dL to 600 mg/dL, a frequency shift of 44 MHz was observed in the resonance frequency of the hybrid sensor called Sensor 1. To show the effect of mutual coupling between the defected ground plane and the FSS on sensitivity parameters in the hybrid sensor structure, a new sensor called Sensor 2 was designed. Sensor 2 has the same geometry and dimensional parameters as Sensor 1 but only consists of a patch antenna with a defected ground plane. A frequency shift of 7 MHz was noted in the resonance frequency of Sensor 2 when the volume percentage of glucose in the glucose-deionized water solutions in the SUT increased from 72 mg/dL to 600 mg/dL. According to the simulation results, the sensitivity of Sensor 1 was calculated as 83.333 kHz/mg dL<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>, while Sensor 2 was 13.258 kHz/mg dL<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>. Thus, it is shown that FSS can be used in antenna-based sensor structures for sensitivity improvement.

articleTitle: Automatic System for Compacting Metal Waste
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The paper presents an automatic system for compacting metal waste from food consumption (boxes or empty cans). The compaction process is found in waste recycling systems. For the compaction system proposed in this paper, there are several automatic control solutions, both in the classic version - with contacts and relays, as well as with PLC. The verification was done through simulation using the dedicated FluidSim software.

articleTitle: Enhanced Backstepping Approach for Diagnosis and Passive Fault Tolerant Control of External Rotor PMSM
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This paper presents a diagnosis method and a passive fault-tolerant control approach for an external-rotor permanent magnet synchronous machine. The control is based on a robust Backstepping control strategy with integral action, based on Lyapunov's stability theorem, and integrated with a vector technique to compensate the impact of the fault. Torque ripples lead to speed fluctuations that affect motor drive performance. A 2D finite element analysis is proposed for fault detection, using coil sensors. This analysis focuses in particular on the specific frequency component of the machine's external magnetic field. The impact of the fault is then compensated for enabling the fault-tolerant control to achieve its objectives. Simulation results are presented to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed fault-tolerant design. The performance of the fault-tolerant control system is evaluated through numerical simulations using MAT-LAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Parameterisation of the Impact Caused by a ‘Salt Tower’ on the Electromagnetic Landscape
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This concerns an experiment to evaluate the hypothesis that “salt towers” (i.e. an outdoor installation developed to produce mineral-rich water droplets in the air that are regarded as having beneficial health effects similar to that of breathing in sea air) may change the local electromagnetic landscape created through the use of public mobile radio-communication base stations networks, i.e. its impact on humans and technical objects. Multi-band measurements of electromagnetic radiation were performed inside and outside a salt tower, to monitor the frequency and spatial pattern of radiation emitted from surrounding base stations. The results were evaluated using various statistical procedures in the context of specific and complex needs that visitors to parks near medical facilities, where salt towers may be frequently found, may have. The results revealed that the level of the electromagnetic exposure and the range of its division were several times lower inside the salt tower, but that its relative time and spatial distribution increased. This confirmed the hypothesis that salt towers may contribute to the control of electromagnetic interference in electronic devices and human exposure, indicating the justification for broader studies near such objects.

articleTitle: Control System Using Shape Memory Alloy for a 3D Printed Robotic Arm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: With the lowering cost of microcontrollers and their improvement on computational power, electronic control can provide more cost-efficient and unconventional methods of actuation for mechanical structures. The recent cost reduction in 3D printing technology allows for further accessibility in terms of design and test of new concepts. In this paper the authors aim for the most cost-efficient implementation of a 3D printed concept of a robotic hand actuated by shape memory alloy (SMA) wires controlled through a software solution which integrates PID regulator. The current work will present details regarding the initial simulations results and the actual implementation.

articleTitle: Application of Power Quality Monitoring for Disturbance and Fault Diagnosis in a Ski Lift Power Supply Installation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: As the integration of renewable generation and smart grid technologies advances, ensuring a reliable power supply and maintaining the power quality within standard limits is critical for the modern power systems. This paper presents a practical application of PQ monitoring strategies to identify and diagnose specific faults or disruptive events in a ski lift power supply installation. The results highlight the importance of comprehensive PQ monitoring and predictive maintenance in improving the reliability of the power systems, particularly for those sections supplying end-users sensitive to electromagnetic disturbances.

articleTitle: A History of the Romanian Transformer Designed, Manufactured and Tested at ELECTROPUTERE Craiova
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This paper is a true history of the birth, rise and demise of the Romanian transformer designed, manufactured and tested at “ELECTROPUTERE” Craiova written by those who lived it to the fullest. It has been planned for a long time, but this year a special occasion came up: 75 years since the founding of Electroputere and 50 years since the founding of ICMET Institute, events that together led to the fame of the Romanian transformer all over the world.

articleTitle: Challenges Related to Renewable Production and Electric Mobility. Part I - Analysis, Solutions and Techno-Sociological Perspectives
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: In the face of current climate challenges and intensified international efforts towards sustainability, issues related to renewable production and electric mobility require an integrated approach of both technical and sociological dimensions. This paper aims to analyze the sociological impact of adopting green technologies, such as electric vehicles and photovoltaic panels, as promising solutions for reducing greenhouse gas emissions and supporting sustainable development. The study underpins a mixed methodology, combining quantitative and qualitative analysis, to explore the perceptions and readiness to adopt these technologies among students at the University of Craiova and their affiliates. It examines these aspects through the lens of five fundamental sociological theories: social change theory, diffusion of innovation theory, social capital theory, socio-technical dynamics and resistance to change. The analysis focuses on the differences and similarities between the two groups, regarding the level of knowledge, motivations and perceived barriers to the use of these technologies. Preliminary results indicate a moderate interest in adopting electric vehicles, with the main barriers being initial costs and underdeveloped infrastructure. On the other hand, photovoltaic panels are perceived as a viable long-term solution, but are deterred by high costs and lack of information. Ultimately, the study emphasizes the importance of education, government support and adequate infrastructure to overcome these obstacles, highlighting the profound role that students play, as agents of change in their communities. Their active involvement improve collaboration between all stakeholders involved in this process, from authorities and academia to the business environment and local communities, thus contributing to the creation of an enabling framework for the implementation of sustainable solutions.

articleTitle: Challenges Related to Renewable Production and Electric Mobility. Part II - Practical Recommendations for Capitalizing the Findings of a Sociological Research on Electric Vehicles and Photovoltaic Panels Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The global transition to green technologies, such as electric vehicles and photovoltaic panels, is an urgent necessity to combat climate change and reduce dependence on fossil resources. This study, part of a larger work based on the exploration of the perceptions and readiness to adopt these technologies among students at the University of Craiova and their affiliates, has a natural continuation, transforming the empirical findings in an action strategy aimed at facilitating Romania's transition to a green economy, reducing carbon emissions and promoting sustainable ecological behavior. By identifying the main barriers, such as high initial costs, insufficiently developed infrastructure and lack of access to information, the research proposes concrete and effective solutions to stimulate the rapid adoption of green technologies. The recommendations mentioned to support the large-scale implementation of environmental solutions include improving infrastructure, conducting information campaigns and offering financial subsidies, thus highlighting the importance of universities as centers of innovation and pillars of change. In addition, collaboration between government, the private sector and local communities is fundamental to creating a sustainable and resilient economy capable of meeting emissions reduction targets. The study's findings highlight the need for an integrated and collaborative approach between all stakeholders involved - academia, government, business environment and local communities - to develop a unified vision of a sustainable future.

articleTitle: The Economic Potential of the Vehicle to the Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: These innovations, along with the natural needs of electrical power generation has brought to a new reality possible - the physical re-displacement of electricity and its bilateral direction of usage - from power grid to user - and from user to power grid. Specifically in the vehicle industry, the Vehicle-to-Grid technology represents a final bonding mechanism between conventional power grid availability and motorized energy transfer: taken when needed, returned when required. The V2G (Vehicle-to-Grid), as the technology is abbreviated - opens for the first time the doors for a new player in the conventional power grid management systems - the energy user itself. Having in hand large power storage units as the electrical vehicles, every household is capable, at nation-wide spread level, to leverage between demand and availability by reversing the consumption direction. As part of the European policy for promotion of environmentally friendly societies, Bulgaria is not an exclusion in the market of electrical driven vehicles. The country however currently experiences a still restricted electrical vehicle usage - mostly due to the underdeveloped charging network - which restricts the usage mainly to larger cities and confined urban areas where shorter routes apply. This study therefore takes into account the inevitable future development of the Electrical Vehicle charging grid, with an overlook on the possibility of a next generation technology introduction, permitting adequate implementation of network augmentation and power grid capacity maximization. We are hereby modelling different scenarios, among which V2G without controlled charging/discharging timings, time-controlled V2G scenarios and opportunistic power grid developments, making usage of both industry controlled and uncontrolled private users G2V (Grid-to-Vehicle) and V2G.

articleTitle: Exploring the Impact of Shading on the Efficiency of Photovoltaic Panels - Part I
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The integration of photovoltaic systems as a source of renewable energy has seen significant growth in recent years due to global sustainability goals. However, the efficiency of these systems is highly influenced by environmental factors, of which shading has been identified as a significant concern. Shading, caused by natural obstacles or man-made structures, can significantly reduce the electricity generation capacity of photovoltaic panel by reducing the amount of solar irradiance incident on the panel's surface. This part of the study aims to investigate the effects of environmental factors on photovoltaic panel performance, focusing on parameters such as output power, voltage and electrical current, as well as efficiency. Through a series of computational simulations and experimental measurements, the research quantifies their impact under different conditions, providing a comprehensive analysis of how these environmental variables influence the operation of photovoltaic panels.

articleTitle: The Unobvious Meanders of the Green Energy Transformation and its (Un)Predictable Consequences, or the Utopia of the “Net Zero” Policy
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The article contains essential technical and economic reservations regarding information disseminated in the media. Journalists and lay “experts” inherently ignore the dynamic and static phenomena resulting from the imbalance in the development of zero-emission sources and their adverse effects on the power system and energy consumers. It also addresses the dilemma of correct development choices and the benefits that result from impartial, objective rationalization of investment decisions in technologies that are actually renewable and strategically available for the country's economy. Also presented are analyses of the lack of sustainable development of technical infrastructures in energy production using examples from Germany, Great Britain, and the United States.

articleTitle: Calculation of the Lifetime of Car Alternators
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: Alternators' lifetimes are determined by the lifetimes of the components: stator, rotor, bearings, voltage regulator, etc. The decommissioning of the alternators is due in approx. 40 % of cases of damage to their insulation systems, their lifetime depending on the operating conditions of the vehicles, respectively on the current drawn, the load of the main engine, the characteristics of the running track, engine vibrations, ambient temperature, solar radiation, humidity, vapors oil, fuel, acid that causes corrosion, etc. This paper presents a method of calculating the lifetimes of the insulation systems of car alternators subjected to constant and time-varying combined thermal and mechanical stresses. It is shown that the consumed lifetimes increase over time and that these increases are directly influenced by the intensification of these increases are directly influenced by the intensification of the stresses above the nominal values are more important if the stresses act simultaneously.

articleTitle: Energy Management Strategy with a Hybrid Renewable Energy System for a Standalone House
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: In the case of standalone houses, ensuring a continuous and regulated power supply from renewable sources is crucial. To address their unpredictable nature, an environmentally conscious hybrid renewable energy system combining photovoltaic panels, a battery, and a Diesel generator is considered. A software application simulates the power flow in a standalone house with common AC loads, analysing summer and winter scenarios over 24 hours. The strategy employed provides an optimal energy management by using the Diesel generator only during peak demand when PV is available and to cover loads and maintain battery life when PV is not in operation. The simulation results provide valuable insights for designing such hybrid energy systems and for enhancing system responsiveness to dynamic energy demands.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study on Prosumers Load Demand and Production Forecasting Using Machine Learning and Time Series Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: A data-driven and realistic policy could overcome the current turmoil in the intricate energy landscape. With solar and wind expanding faster than liquified natural gas or nuclear ever have, local, bottom-up solutions, such as organising collaboratively residential prosumers into electricity trading communities and the efficient use of aggregators, are one way to resilience and control over these resources. This paper analyses the features and characteristics of some prosumers and facilitates the identification of relevant algorithms for the specific tasks of both load demand and production forecasting using machine learning and time series techniques, thus enabling them to operate on a level playing field in the market. Load demand and production forecast simulations on two data sets, one collected in 2019, corresponding to 50 residential households and a public building from Portugal, and the other from 2023, that aggregates values from 29 household prosumers from Romania, show that both simple and double exponential smoothing techniques are more accurate than Markov predictors. Provided that the external contingencies influencing either the consumption or the production are considered, the latter gives a better prediction accuracy for energy production, whereas the former provides a better forecast for the consumption.

articleTitle: Simulation Algorithms for Dynamic Models. Case Study: AHU Control
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: In this work the use of a simulation algorithm based on the approximation of the transfer functions by difference equations is proposed. This algorithm is compared with four other algorithms based on the use of numerical methods for the solution of a multivariable nonlinear model with Hammerstein-Wiener structure, whose linear part is made up of four transfer functions. Using two data sets from different experiments, it is shown that the proposed algorithm is faster than the others, while maintaining accuracy, and is also suitable for the simulation of the closed-loop control of the system.

articleTitle: Mathematical Considerations Regarding the Maximum Power Transfer in Inductive Power Transfer Circuits
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The study of wireless power transfer systems has been a continuous concern of scientists in the last years. This was due to the development of technologies in the field and the increase of the number of electronic applications that use the principle of wireless power supply. The inductive power transfer systems have experienced the greatest development up to now, their study being still a current topic. The present work aimed to add a contribution to the theoretical study regarding the inductive power transfer circuits by performing some exact mathematical calculations regarding the identification of the conditions for obtaining a maximum active power transferred to the load. Different situations were considered. The results obtained by calculation were interpreted in correlation with the real functioning of the system. This study completes the known theory in the field.

articleTitle: A New Approach to Energy Efficiency Evaluation of Induction Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The paper presents two important aspects of the energy efficiency evaluation of induction motors: the performance of a comparative analysis between the energy efficiency of an induction motor powered by two categories of sources - purely sinusoidal symmetrical three-phase source, respectively, frequency converter, and also, a new way of finding the energy efficiency of induction motors - in case of using frequency converters (and the existence of harmonics) - starting from the determination of the fractal dimension of the variation curves of the applied voltage, currents in the windings and the developed electromagnetic torque. The stated purpose is to show the influence of non-uniformity degree of the specific parameters of the induction motor, supplied by power electronics, on its energy efficiency - through a simple law - and to open the possibility of online evaluation of the energy efficiency in case of drive systems with continuously monitored induction motors. The entire study was carried out using PSIM and MATLAB software (to determine the fractal dimension).
